title: POC scoping - workload modeling for Terranet Payments
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-08 09:00 AM PT | Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Jordan Mills (Redwood AE), Priya Kohli (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM) — Marcus Lee, Aisha Rahman, Derek O'Neal, Priya Sen (Terranet)

Summary: Initial POC scoping to align on workload characterization and traffic modeling for a 6-week POC. Focus on QPS, concurrency, input/output token distribution, latency SLOs, and data residency/security needs. Agreed to run two benchmark suites (synthetic and replay) and produce cost/throughput projection.

[00:00] Jordan Mills: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Uh I'm Jordan from Redwood, on the AE side, and with me is Priya our infra SE, and Lena on CSM. 
[00:12] Marcus Lee: Hey Jordan, thanks, yeah we wanted to get into the weeds on how you all size things for payments flows and what success looks like.
[00:20] Priya Kohli: Great. Quick agenda: confirm workload profile (qps & concurrency), token distribution (input vs output), latency/throughput targets, data residency and security checks, and then scope benchmarks and timeline for the POC.
[00:33] Aisha Rahman: Sounds good. To set context, Terranet processes authorization and reconciliation flows, so we have both synchronous low-latency API calls and batch reconciliation jobs. Most critical is authorization path — sub-second where possible.
[00:47] Derek O'Neal: Right, the auth path is ~70% of calls but small payloads, and then we get a long-tail of reconciliation queries that can be bigger.
[01:05] Priya Kohli: Can you quantify QPS and concurrency for us — ballpark numbers? That helps us pick hosting mode and whether Dedicated is needed.
[01:13] Marcus Lee: Sure — steady-state traffic is around 120 QPS average, peaks up to 800 QPS during batch windows (mostly short, 5-10 minutes). Concurrency on the auth path is ~200 concurrent requests at peak. The reconciliation jobs are batched — about 30 jobs/hr with large payloads.
[01:35] Jordan Mills: Good, that helps. What's your current model for inference? Is it on-prem or cloud? Any preference for hosted vs Dedicated for the POC?
[01:42] Aisha Rahman: We run a hybrid — core services in our VPC on cloud, some older infra on prem. For POC we prefer Private (VPC) because of PCI scoping and we need audit logs.
[01:53] Priya Kohli: Understood. For PCI-adjacent workloads we typically recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with VPC peering + KMS. We'll capture the exact compliance needs.
[02:05] Priya Sen: On tokens: input messages are typically short — auth request text ~15-40 tokens. Output is also small for the decision output — a couple tokens. Reconciliation prompts can be longer: input ~400-1200 tokens and output ~200-600 tokens.
[02:36] Priya Kohli: Great — so two distinct distributions. Small (auth) and large (recon). That matters a lot: batching and model selection will differ.
[02:45] Marcus Lee: And the SLA: P50 under 200 ms for auth ideally, P95 under 500 ms. We understand some variability, but that's our target.
[03:10] Priya Kohli: For P50/P95 at that QPS, we need to consider both model latency and the end-to-end network/PVC overhead. For the small auth calls, continuous batching actually can hurt latency if batch windows are long — so we may use single-request fast paths. For recon we can enable larger batching to improve cost.
[03:29] Jordan Mills: Quick question — do you have an internal SLA for retries or fallback? If we need to fall back to a cached decision or a simpler rule, how should POC measure functional availability?
[03:40] Derek O'Neal: We do have a fallback to rule-based scoring for critical failures, but we want to test degradation behavior in the POC.
[04:00] Priya Kohli: OK we'll include a graceful degradation plan: measuring percent of requests served by primary model vs fallback, and tail latencies during simulated load spikes.
[04:09] Aisha Rahman: On security — we require KMS, customer-managed keys for the private deploy, full audit logs for model input/outputs stored for 30 days, and SOC2 maturity level.
[04:21] Lena Ortiz: We can share Redwood's SOC2 and ISO docs and propose an audit log schema. For POC we can enable encrypted logging and restricted access.
[04:30] Marcus Lee: Good. Can you also show token-level cost estimates? We need to compare hosted vs dedicated vs private cost curves.
[04:39] Jordan Mills: Yes, we'll produce cost-per-1M tokens and projected monthly spend for your projected traffic.
[05:00] Priya Sen: For traffic modeling, we can provide a replay of production traces for the POC if you need to run realistic benchmarks. We can scrub PII.
[05:08] Priya Kohli: That would be ideal — replay lets us validate KV cache hit rates, prefix caching, and realistic token distribution. The other approach is synthetic stress tests to push p95/p99.
[05:20] Marcus Lee: We'll do both. We'll provide a 24-hour sampled trace and a synthetic high-load script to exercise spikes.
[06:00] Priya Kohli: OK next let's sketch POC benchmarks: (1) Functional validation — correctness on a sample of prompts and accuracy metrics; (2) Latency and throughput benchmarks — p50/p95/p99 under steady-state and spike; (3) Cost benchmarking — cost per 1M tokens and per-request; (4) Resilience — failover to fallback and behavior under node loss.
[06:20] Jordan Mills: Timeline — propose 6 weeks: Week 0 onboarding & infra prep, Week 1 replay and synthetic benchmark runs, Week 2 model tuning and quantization tests, Week 3 dedicated performance runs, Week 4 integration and security review, Week 5 acceptance tests and business criteria evaluation, Week 6 wrap + decision.
[07:10] Aisha Rahman: That seems fine but we need an acceleration option to 4 weeks if legal and infra approvals move fast.
[07:18] Jordan Mills: We can compress by parallelizing infra setup and initial benchmarks. We'll document prerequisites (VPC peering, KMS keys, SSO access).
[07:50] Derek O'Neal: For the model, do you recommend one of Redwood's verified open models or bring our own fine-tuned model? We have an internal fine-tuned model for transaction classification.
[07:36] Priya Kohli: Both are options. For throughput benchmarking we'll use a standard open model variant for baseline, and then run your fine-tuned model in a later stage. Quantized variants may dramatically reduce GPU footprint.
[07:48] Marcus Lee: Good. Any guidance on GPU sizing for 800 QPS peaks?
[07:55] Priya Kohli: Rough calc: with small token lengths and a low-latency model, each GPU can saturate ~1,200-1,500 small auth QPS if using optimized kernels and NVLink on certain instances. But that's model and hw dependent. For mixed workload (some large recon) you'll need capacity planning that separates low-latency pools from bulk batch pools or uses model variants with different quantization.
[08:40] Priya Sen: Does Redwood support routing policy so auth goes to low-latency pool and recon to batch?
[08:45] Jordan Mills: Yes we have smart routing and can set policy by route, latency target, or model variant. We'll add recommended routing config to the POC runbook.
[09:10] Marcus Lee: On measurements — can you capture token distribution stats and KV cache hit rate? That's critical to understand cost.
[09:17] Priya Kohli: Absolutely. We'll instrument per-route metrics: tokens in/out, tokens per request histogram, KV cache hits, batch sizes, and per-token time.
[09:45] Aisha Rahman: For acceptance criteria, here's what we propose: auth path p50 <= 200 ms and p95 <= 500 ms; functional match rate >= 98% vs our current model for a sample set; cost <= X (we'll add target after you send token cost estimates); audit logs available and encrypted; and an integration checklist completed.
[10:03] Jordan Mills: We'll formalize that as the POC acceptance criteria. We'll also run a regression evaluation with your test set to measure quality delta.
[10:35] Priya Kohli: For the benchmarking approach: Step A — small request latency microbench (no batching), Step B — steady-state load at 120 QPS, Step C — spike test to 800 QPS for 10 minutes, Step D — replay of 24-hour sample, Step E — large-batch recon throughput test. We'll provide scripts and a benchmark dashboard.
[11:12] Derek O'Neal: Competitors — we did quick evals with Anthropic and some managed endpoints; cost and routing flexibility were weaker in those tests. We'll likely compare results across OpenAI hosted endpoints, Anthropic, and a self-host baseline.
[11:50] Lena Ortiz: Logistics: we'll need access to a sandbox account, service account keys, and a scrubbed trace. We'll also set up a shared benchmark sheet — we can link to it.
[12:22] Aisha Rahman: We'll aim to provide those within 5 business days.
[13:15] Jordan Mills: 1) Redwood to send POC runbook, cost estimates, recommended infra (VPC peering + KMS), and benchmark scripts. 2) Terranet to provide scrubbed 24-hour trace, service account, and decision criteria doc. 3) Schedule kick-off for next Monday pending infra access.

Notes: transcript contains small transcription artifacts (speaker overlaps, occasional mis-heard acronyms like "KV cash" in one dev note). References shared: https://redwood.example.com/poc-runbook (POC runbook), https://shared.example.com/benchmarks/terranet (benchmark spreadsheet), Redwood SOC2/ISO packet link: https://redwood.example.com/security/docs
summary: POC scoping focused on workload characterization: Terranet has two traffic modes (small low-latency auth: ~120 avg QPS, peaks 800 QPS, and large batch reconciliation jobs). Agreed private/VPC deployment for POC due to PCI adjacency. Benchmarks: latency/throughput, replay, synthetic spike, and cost comparisons vs competitors. 6-week POC proposed with options to compress to 4 weeks. Acceptance criteria drafted (auth p50 <=200ms, p95 <=500ms, functional match >=98%).
action_items: Jordan Mills - Send POC runbook, infra checklist, and pricing estimates (due 2026-10-13)
Terranet (Marcus) - Provide scrubbed 24-hour trace and service account for sandbox (due 2026-10-13)
Priya Kohli - Prepare benchmark scripts and recommended routing config (due 2026-10-12)
Lena Ortiz - Share SOC2 packet and audit schema for logs (due 2026-10-12)
next_steps: Redwood to share detailed cost per 1M tokens and projected monthly cost for Terranet traffic
Set up kickoff meeting once sandbox access and keys provided
Run initial microbench and steady-state tests within Week 1 of POC
